title: Facing Issues with 2FA (Two-Factor Authentication)?
content:
TL;DR:
If your 2FA code isn’t working, first ensure you are entering it quickly, as codes refresh every 30 seconds. Always use your authenticator app (like Google Authenticator) instead of searching for codes in your email, since email codes are not valid for 2FA login.
If issues continue, try resetting and reconfiguring your authenticator app by removing old entries and initiating a fresh 2FA setup with the new QR code. You can also clear your browser’s cache and cookies, switch to a different browser, or even log in from another device to isolate the problem.
If none of these steps resolve the issue, remove FundedNext 2FA from your authenticator app and re-add it following the correct process.
If you're experiencing trouble while using
Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)
, here are some recommended steps to help resolve the issue:
​
Why is the 2FA code not working?
There could be several reasons your 2FA code isn’t working properly. Here are some steps to troubleshoot:
Enter the Code Quickly
2FA codes refresh every 30 seconds. Please make sure to enter the code promptly before it expires.
Use the Authenticator App, Not Email
Many traders mistakenly search for codes in their email. Please
only use the code from your authenticator app
(like Google Authenticator), as email codes are not valid for 2FA login.
Reset and Reconfigure the Authenticator App
If the code still doesn’t work, try this:
Remove all existing entries related to our platform from your authenticator app.
Log in to your account again and
initiate a fresh 2FA setup
using the new QR code provided.
This ensures that your device is properly synced with our system.
Clear Your Browser’s Cache and Cookies
Sometimes, saved data in your browser can cause login issues. Try clearing your cache and cookies before retrying.
Try a Different Browser
If the problem continues, switching to another browser might help isolate the issue.
Use a Different Device
If none of the above steps work, please try logging in from another device to see if the issue persists.
How to Remove FundedNext 2FA from Your Authenticator App?
Step 1: Open Your Authenticator App
Launch the app you currently use for 2FA (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, Authy, etc.).
Step 2: Find the FundedNext Entry
Scroll through your list of accounts and look for any entries labeled “FundedNext.” It should be like this: "FundedNext: your email address."
Step 3: Delete/Remove the Entry
Tap and hold (or swipe left/right) on the FundedNext entry.
A “Delete” or “Remove” option should appear.
Confirm the removal.
Step 4: Double-Check
Make sure no other FundedNext-related entries remain in your authenticator app.
For better visualization, here is a short video:
If you've tried all the above steps and still can't access your account, please reach out to our
support team
for further assistance. We're here to help!
​
​
​
Note:
2FA can only be disabled once. Once it's turned off manually for you, then it cannot be disabled again in the future.

TLDR:
Stellar Instant Accounts have
no daily loss limit
but use a
trailing maximum loss limit
of
6%
. This starts from your initial balance and moves up only when you make profits, never exceeding your starting balance. Losses do not reduce it. If your equity falls below this limit, your account is breached. The rule is designed to encourage steady growth while preventing excessive losses.
There are no Daily Loss Limits in Stellar Instant Accounts. However, there is a Maximum Loss Limit of 6%, which follows the trailing loss limit method.
Trailing Maximum Loss Limit (How It Works)
Let’s break it down with an example:
Account Size
: $10,000
Initial Trailing Maximum Loss Limit (6%)
: $600
This means if your equity drops below
$9,400
, your account will be breached.

$200 profit
.
New balance: $10,200
MLL level = $10,200 - $600 = $9600;
Greater than the current trailing MLL
Trailing Maximum Loss Limit:
$9,600
2nd Trade
:
You lost
$100
.
New balance: $10,100
MLL level = $10,100 - $600 = $9500;
Not greater than the current trailing MLL
Maximum Loss Limit stays at
$9,600
Losses do not change the Maximum Loss Limit—it only grows with profit.
3rd Trade
:
You made a
$400 profit
.
New balance: $10,500
MLL level = $10,500 - $600 = $9,900;
Greater than the current trailing MLL
Maximum Loss Limit rises to
$9,900

:
You made a
$600 profit
.
New balance: $11,100
MLL level = $11,100 - $600 = $10,500;
Greater than the current trailing MLL
Maximum Loss Limit rises to
$10,000.
The Maximum Loss Limit range will not go over your account's initial balance. So your Maximum Loss Limit is now
$10,000
.
Important Rule:
Even if you keep making profit, your trailing Maximum Loss Limit can never go above your initial balance, which is $10,000. So, even though the calculation showed $10,500, the actual Maximum Loss Limit is capped at $10,000. The Maximum Loss Limit does not reset after receiving a performance reward.

title: Is There a Scale‑Up Plan for Stellar Instant Accounts?
content:
Yes.
FundedNext’s Stellar Instant Account includes a performance-based scale-up plan that can grow your account up to
10× your initial balance
as you consistently perform and make withdrawals.
How the Scale-Up Plan Works for Stellar Instant?
To qualify for a scale-up in your current tier, you must:
Achieve
cumulative 10% growth
in the current tier, measured as;
(
Total disbursed withdrawal amount ÷ current tier start balance) x 100
.
​
Complete
at least one withdrawal
in the current tier.
Once both conditions are met, your
account balance
and
maximum loss limit
increase, and your
tier is upgraded
.
Updated Reward Share (profit split):
Tier 1–2:
70%
Tier 3 and onward:
80%
(capped)
Your Reward Share increases to 80% by Tier 3 and remains fixed at 80% from there. After that, only the account balance and tier continue to grow.
Stellar Instant Tier Tables
Assumptions for the examples below
Initial account balance used for illustration:
$10,000
.
“Wallet Transfer” = profit amount eligible for split.
“Withdrawal Growth” =
(Total disbursed withdrawal amount ÷ current tier start balance) x 100
.
“Max Loss Limit” will equal the
Tier's Initial Balance and will follow the trailing method.
A) When a Trader Withdraws the Full Eligible Reward Share from a $10,000 Account (Tier 1)
Thus, withdrawing the full eligible Reward Share in a single Tier-1 cycle results in
7%
growth (below the required 10%), so
no scale-up
is granted, and based on MLL calculations, the account will be considered
breached
for withdrawing the full amount.
​
B) When a Trader Does Not Withdraw the Full Eligible Reward Share from a $10,000 Account
Tier 1 reward share-70%
Here, the trader becomes eligible for a scale-up after his 4th cycle. So he will start the 5th cycle with $20,200.
Note: The growth of the account from the 5th cycle will be based on ($10,000 + $10,000)
New Reward Share: 70%
​
Again, in the 6th cycle, the trader is eligible for a scale-up, which would add another $10,000 to the account balance in the 7th cycle, making the cycle's starting balance $30,250.
Note: The growth of the account from the 7th cycle will be based on ($20,000 + $10,000).
The new Reward Share: 80%.
​
Cumulative withdrawal growth in Tier 3 exceeds 10% ⇒
Scale-Up to Tier 4.
From here, the Reward Share
remains 80%
, and the account can continue scaling tier-by-tier (subject to the same criteria) up to
10×
the initial balance. After reaching 10× the initial balance, clients may be eligible to grow their account balance up to
$2,000,000
.
The Post-Tier 10 Journey
Once you successfully reach Tier 10, your growth journey doesn't stop. The scaling process continues to follow our standard
Scale-Up
criteria in a repeating cycle.
However, traders with Stellar Instant Accounts
purchased or reset on or after January 12, 2026
will follow the new
Scale-Up program
.
This allows you to consistently increase your account size until you reach the maximum
$2 million limit
. Please note that during this continued scaling phase, only the account balance is updated at each subsequent stage.
Notes
Reward Share updated:
70% in Tiers 1–2
,
80% from Tier 3 onward
(capped).
The 10% growth test
uses
withdrawals actually disbursed
in the tier relative to the tier’s start balance.
At least one withdrawal
is required in each tier to qualify for scale-up.
Maximum Loss Limit Balance
in the tables is shown equal to the
tier's initial  balance.
Scale-up increment
follows the Stellar Instant Account’s rule of adding the
initial balance
at each upgrade. If your implementation also carries forward retained growth into the next tier’s starting balance, you can reflect that in the “Cycle Start Balance” column for the next tier.
Account balance and tier will keep increasing to 10x of your account size as long as the criteria are met each time. Afterward, clients will be eligible to grow their account balance up to $2 million.

title: Does FundedNext offer Swap-Free accounts?
content:
FundedNext offers swap-free accounts across every challenge, allowing traders to
hold positions overnight without any swap or rollover fees
. These accounts have the same spreads, leverage, and rules as regular accounts, and no additional paperwork is required to activate them. The swap-free option is ideal for clients looking to avoid extra costs or those whose personal or religious beliefs prevent them from paying or receiving interest.
Also, by eliminating the overnight holding charges, you can ensure trades that are within your Daily Loss Limit aren’t pushed into a breach by rollover fees. Here’s an example:
Scenario: Account breach due to swap (BTCUSD)
You have a $
100,000 Stellar 2-Step Account;
Daily Loss Limit = $5,000
. You placed a
BUY
trade of
1 lot
on
BTCUSD
at
102,000.00
. By the end of day, the price is
97,030.00
Floating PnL before swap
Floating PnL = (97,030.00 − 102,000.00) × 0.10 × 1
= (−49,700 pips × $0.10 × 1 lot)
=
−$4,970.00
Overnight holding charge
Swap =
−$42.00
Total Daily Loss
= −$4,970.00 + (−$42.00)
=
−$5,012.00
Outcome:
The floating loss was just under the limit, but the
swap
pushed the day’s total to
−$5,012
, triggering an account breach.
However, with a
swap-free account
, your floating loss remains −$4,970.00, keeping you safely under the Daily Loss Limit and avoiding a breach.
Please note that the pricing for
swap-free
accounts is
10% higher
than regular accounts, as FundedNext covers the cost of overnight holding charges usually borne by clients.

title: How does the Add-On feature work with the FundedNext new Challenge purchase?
content:
The Add-On feature in FundedNext's new Challenge purchase is an optional enhancement that traders can choose to apply to their trading plan. This feature is designed to provide greater flexibility and potential benefits to our traders.
FundedNext is offering eight Add-Ons:
Swap-Free Add-On, Lifetime Reward 95% Add-On, No Minimum Trading Days Add-On, 150% Reward Add-On, Bi-Weekly Reward Add-On, Maximum Loss Limit 10% Add-On, Double Up Add-On
, and
On-Demand Rewards Add-On.
Swap-Free Add-On
When selecting their preferred Challenge, traders have the option to choose between a
Swap
or
Swap-Free
Add-On.
Swap Account:
A
Swap
account in forex trading involves the interest that is paid or earned for holding a position overnight.
Swap-Free Account:
A
Swap-Free
account is designed for traders who do not want to earn or pay interest for holding a position overnight.
If a trader opts for a Swap-Free Add-On, it incurs an additional 10% fee on top of their chosen Challenge price.
For example, if traders want to purchase a Stellar 2-Step $100,000 Challenge Account priced at $549.00, once they select the Swap-Free Add-On, the price will be $604.00 (10% increase).
On-Demand Rewards Add-On
When you purchase this Add-On during your Challenge Phase, you unlock a bundle of significant benefits for your trading journey:
On-Demand Performance Rewards:
Request your Reward Share on any day once you meet the eligibility criteria.
95% Reward Share:
Increase your Reward Share to 95% from your very first Reward on the FundedNext Account.
40% Consistency Rule:
Applies specifically to your FundedNext Account.
Traders with this Add-On do not have to wait for a fixed schedule to request their Performance Reward. Once you have transitioned to a FundedNext Account, you can request a Performance Reward at any day, provided the profit on your FundedNext Account is at least 2% of your initial account balance while maintaining the 40% consistency rule.
Once your request is submitted, rewards are processed and disbursed within
24 hours
, ensuring you have quick access to your Reward Share.
Understanding the 40% Consistency Rule
The On-Demand Rewards Add-On includes a 40% Consistency Rule that applies specifically to the FundedNext Account. This rule ensures that your trading performance is balanced rather than being reliant on a single trade or day.
The Rule:
Your best trading day's profit should not exceed 40% of your total generated profit; this is not a daily profit cap, it only applies at the point of your on-demand reward request.
Example:
On a $50,000 Stellar 2-Step FundedNext Account, suppose you have a total profit of $2,000. This meets the minimum 2% account growth requirement ($1,000) needed to request a Performance Reward.
Day 1: $500 profit
Day 2: $750 profit
Day 3: $750 profit
Your best day ($750) is 37.5% of your $2,000 total, below the 40% threshold, meaning you are fully compliant and eligible to request your Performance Reward.
Which account types can use this add-on?
The On-Demand Rewards add-on is available for Stellar Lite, Stellar 1-Step, and Stellar 2-Step accounts.
What is the cost of this add-on?
This add-on is optional and can be selected during the checkout process for an additional 5% of the account's base registration fee.
When can I make my first request?
You can request your Performance Reward on any day your FundedNext Account has grown by at least 2% of the initial balance and you have maintained the 40% consistency rule. Once your request is submitted, rewards are processed and disbursed within 24 hours, ensuring you have quick access to your Reward Share.
What if I can not maintain the 40% consistency rule?
Maintaining the 40% consistency rule is required to be eligible for a Performance Reward request when using the On-Demand Rewards Add-On.
If you are unable to maintain the 40% Consistency Rule by the end of your trading cycle, the following will apply:
If your account is in profit:
Your trading cycle will be extended, giving you the opportunity to continue trading and meet the consistency rule before submitting a reward request.
If your account is not in profit:
Standard account conditions will apply. To learn more about what happens to an account at the end of a trading cycle, please refer to
this article
.
Final Important Points
You will
not
be able to submit a Performance Reward request until the 40% Consistency Rule is met, regardless of your account's profit level.
If you are eligible for an On-Demand Reward but choose not to request it, your trading cycle will
continue to extend
. The cycle will only conclude once you submit your reward request.
If you become eligible for an On-Demand Reward but do not request it and subsequently
break the consistency rule
, your cycle will be extended until you are eligible to request an On-Demand Reward again.
In short, if you have purchased the On-Demand Rewards Add-On, requesting the On-Demand Rewards is the only way to conclude your trading cycle. There are no alternative options available to request the Performance Reward from your account.
Lifetime Reward 95% Add-On
The Lifetime Reward 95% Add-On is a significant enhancement that allows traders to receive a higher percentage of their earnings. When you opt for this Add-On, you are entitled to a 95% reward share of their profits.
In the Stellar 1-Step, Stellar 2-Step, and Stellar Lite Accounts, the initial Performance Reward from the FundedNext Account starts at 80%. However, if your account is under this Add-On, then the lifetime Reward will be 95% from the FundedNext Account.
If traders opt for the Lifetime Reward 95% Add-On, it will incur an additional 25% fee for the Stellar 1-Step Account and an additional 30% fee for Stellar Lite, and Stellar 2-Step Accounts on top of their selected Challenge price.
​
For example, if traders want to purchase a Stellar 2-Step $100,000 Challenge Account priced at $549.00, once they select the Lifetime Reward 95% Add-On, the price will be $713.7 (a 30% increase).
A trader needs to keep in mind that, once the FundedNext Account is eligible for Scale Up, the account balance will be increased to 40% of the initial balance, and the reward share percentage will remain the same at 95%.
No Minimum Trading Days
The '
No Minimum Trading Days
' Add-On removes the minimum 5-day trading rule from the Stellar 1-Step Account, Stellar 2-Step Account, and Stellar Lite Account. This means that when a trader purchases this Add-On, they will not have to wait for 5 days to pass the Stellar 1-Step, Stellar 2-Step, and Stellar Lite Challenges.
If traders opt for the '
No Minimum Trading Days
' Add-On, it will incur an additional
25%
fee for Stellar 1-Step, and Stellar 2-Step Accounts and an additional
20%
fee for Stellar Lite Accounts, on top of their selected Challenge price.

Reward

Accounts.

Bi-Weekly Reward

This means that when a trader opts for this Add-On, they are not required to wait for 21 days before requesting a Performance Reward from the Stellar Lite, and Stellar 2-Step FundedNext Accounts. 25%
fee for Stellar 2-Step Accounts and an additional
15%
fee for Stellar Lite Accounts, on top of their selected Challenge price.

All Stellar Lite Account Models

' Add-On, the price will be $148.75 (a 25% increase).

The

This Add-On will cost the trader 25% more of the base price of the Account, which means traders will have to pay 25% extra for this Add-On. As mentioned, this can only be added to the Account during purchase of the Stellar Lite Challenge.

For example, if a trader acquires a Stellar 2-Step $100,000 Challenge Account with any Add-On, the second Challenge Account that he will receive after passing the Challenge Phase will have the default account with no Add-Ons.

title: Is News Trading Allowed in the Stellar 1-Step Account?
content:
TL;DR:
Yes, news trading is allowed in the Stellar 1-Step Challenge and FundedNext Account. However, once you reach the
FundedNext Account
, a special
News Profit Split Rule
applies: only
40% of profits
made within 5 minutes before and after a
high-impact news event
will be counted toward your account. Losses remain fully your responsibility.
Yes,
news trading is permitted
across all account types at FundedNext — including the
Stellar 1-Step Challenge Account
and
FundedNext Account
.
However, traders must
carefully follow specific guidelines
, especially after reaching the FundedNext Account.
What’s Allowed
You can trade during news events in both the Challenge Account and FundedNext Account.
You may also hold running trades during news events without restrictions.
No restrictions apply during low-impact or unrelated news events.
News Profit Split Rule (FundedNext Account Only)
Once you receive the
FundedNext Account
, trades executed during high-impact news events are subject to this
profit adjustment rule
:
Time Window
Applies to trades opened or closed within 5 minutes before and after a listed high-impact news event.
This creates a 10-minute window where the rule is active.
Profit Adjustment
Only 40% of the profit from trades during this window will be counted toward your account balance.
Losses during this window are fully applied and not adjusted.
Applicable To
Both market execution trades and pending orders, including SL and TP triggers.
Partial Closures
If you partially close a trade during the news window, the entire trade will be affected — only 40% of the profit will be counted.
Impact on Performance Reward and Account Status
The adjusted profit will affect your reward eligibility and net profit for the cycle.
If your account ends below the initial balance after adjustment, you cannot request a withdrawal.
Example Calculation:
Positive Scenario
Total profit excluding news trades: $10,000
Profit from news trades: $3,000
News profit counted: 40% of $3,000 = $1,200
Final account profit = $10,000 + $1,200 = $11,200
Loss Scenario with Adjustment Reset
Initial Balance: $100,000
End Balance: $101,000
Account value excluding news profit: $98,000
News profit: $3,000 → 40% = $1,200
Adjusted balance: $98,000 + $1,200 = $99,200
Since the adjusted balance is below $100,000, no withdrawal is allowed.
However, next cycle will start from the original $100,000 balance (reset benefit granted in this case).
When Does the News Rule Apply?
Only during listed high-impact news events that directly correlate with the traded pair.
Example:
EUR/USD during USD or EUR high-impact news = Rule applies
EUR/USD during CNY news = No rule applies
Please trade responsibly during news events. FundedNext is not liable for losses incurred due to volatility during these periods.

title: What are the Risk Violation Types?
content:
TL;DR:
Risk violations occur when no Stop Loss is placed at all (No SL Trade), when a single trade exceeds the maximum allowable risk (High Risk), or when multiple open trades together exceed the total cumulative risk limit (At-a-Time High Risk).
This guide provides technical explanations for common trade violations. Understanding these terms will help you ensure your trading activity remains compliant with our guidelines.
This guide provides technical explanations for common trade violations. Understanding these terms will help you ensure your trading activity remains compliant with our guidelines.
What is a "No SL Trade"?
This indicates that a trade was executed and closed without ever having a Stop Loss order in place. FundedNext requires a Stop Loss to be placed on every trade. Trades that run and close without one are flagged under this violation type.
How is "High Risk" defined for an individual trade?
A trade is flagged as "High Risk" if its individual risk exposure exceeds the maximum allowable risk limit established in the trading rules. The risk on each trade is calculated against the initial account balance based on Stop Loss placement and the maximum potential loss on that trade.
What does "At-a-Time High Risk" mean?
While individual trades might stay within permitted risk limits, this violation occurs when the combined risk exposure of all open trades at the same time exceeds the maximum cumulative risk threshold. FundedNext evaluates total risk across all open positions simultaneously, not per trade in isolation.

title: Is scalping allowed in FundedNext?
content:
TLDR:
Yes, scalping is allowed at FundedNext. However, tick scalping, which involves extremely rapid-fire trades aimed at exploiting micro price movements, is strictly prohibited due to its potential for abuse and market disruption.
Scalping is Allowed, but with Limitations
FundedNext supports various trading styles, including
scalping
, as long as the strategy aligns with our
fair use policies
and
does not involve abusive practices
.
Scalping
means entering and exiting trades quickly (within minutes) to take advantage of small price moves.
It is permitted in both
Challenge Accounts
and
FundedNext Accounts
.
Manual and algorithmic scalping are allowed as long as they don’t resemble tick-level exploitation.
What is Tick Scalping and Why is it  Not Allowed?
Tick scalping
is an ultra-fast strategy where traders attempt to profit from minute price changes, often just a few ticks, using automation and ultra-fast execution speeds.
Key Characteristics of Tick Scalping:
High-frequency, low-duration trades:
Trades last seconds or milliseconds.
Automated execution:
Often relies on EAs or bots.
Micro-profit targeting:
Aims for profits of just a few pips/ticks per trade.
Order flooding:
Generates rapid buy/sell positions that may manipulate order books or market pricing.
Why FundedNext Prohibits Tick Scalping:
Unfair advantage:
Exploits price movement before other traders can react.
Market disruption:
Creates artificial volatility and can front-run slower participants.
Server strain:
The high frequency of trades and cancellations burdens the trading system.
Example of Prohibited Tick Scalping
A trader uses a bot to open and close positions on XAUUSD within milliseconds, repeatedly targeting 0.1 pip movements.
While it may appear to be harmless micro-profit trading, this behavior disrupts pricing, liquidity, and server performance, and therefore
violates FundedNext rules
.
Trade Responsibly
While scalping is a legitimate strategy, traders must
avoid tick-based automation
and
excessive high-frequency activity
. FundedNext encourages all traders to focus on
consistent, fair, and ethical trading behavior
.
If you’re unsure whether your strategy is allowed, it’s best to
review our
Prohibited Trading Strategy Policy
for full details.

title: What is the IBAN  of FundedNext?
content:
An International Bank Account Number (IBAN) is a standardized international code used to identify bank accounts across national borders. It helps in facilitating cross-border payments by making the process more efficient and less error-prone. An IBAN contains information about the country, the bank, and the account number.
What are the differences between an account number and an IBAN?
The key difference between an account number and an IBAN lies in their scope and structure. An account number is a unique identifier for a bank account within a specific bank in a country. It is usually a series of digits, and its format varies from bank to bank. On the other hand, an IBAN is internationally recognized and includes additional details like the country code and check digits. This makes it more detailed and standardized for international transactions.
How many digits should be there in an IBAN?
The length of an IBAN can vary between countries, ranging from 14 to 34 alphanumeric characters. However, the most common lengths are between 20 to 24 characters. Each country has a fixed length for its IBAN format.
Is SWIFT/BIC required if IBAN is there?
Although IBANs are designed to uniquely identify bank accounts for international transactions, the SWIFT/BIC code is also often required. The SWIFT/BIC code identifies the specific bank where the account is held. While the IBAN provides the account number and country, the SWIFT/BIC provides information about the bank and branch, making it crucial for processing international transactions efficiently.
How to handle a 23-digit IBAN when the payer's bank requires a 24-digit IBAN for payment?
In cases where there's a mismatch in the number of digits required for an IBAN (e.g., the payee's IBAN is 23 digits, but the payer's bank system requires 24), it's essential to:
Verify the IBAN:
Ensure that the provided IBAN is correct and complete.
Contact the Payer’s Bank:
Discuss the discrepancy with the bank to seek a solution. They may have a procedure for handling such cases.
Contact the Payee’s Bank:
Inquire if there's any specific format or additional information required for international transfers.
Consider Using a Bank Identifier Code (BIC):
Sometimes, including the bank's BIC along with the IBAN may resolve the issue.
Explore Alternative Transfer Methods:
If the issue persists, consider using different transfer services that can accommodate the given IBAN length.
Alternative Method:
Using SWIFT/BIC and Account Number

title: When does my trading cycle start?
content:
At FundedNext, a trader's trading cycle starts when they make their first trade, not when their account is activated.
For example, if a trader receives their account on a Sunday and makes their first trade on a Wednesday, the trading cycle begins on Wednesday, not Sunday.

. For the remainder of the year, when daylight saving time is not in effect, the server time is adjusted to GMT +2.

title: How can I calculate the Maximum Loss Limit?
content:
For traders participating in the Stellar 2-Step Challenge, the Maximum Loss Limit is 10% of their initial account balance. On the other hand, for traders enrolled in the Stellar 1-Step Challenge, the Maximum Loss Limit is 6% of their initial account balance.
Additionally, for traders participating in the Stellar Lite Challenge, the Maximum Loss Limit is 8% of their initial account balance.
Let's consider an example to illustrate this calculation. Suppose you have purchased a Stellar 2-Step Account $100,000. Here's how the calculation works:
Case 01:
Suppose you start with a $100,000 account, and your Maximum Loss Limit is set at 10% ($10,000). This means that if your account balance/equity ever drops below $90,000, it will be considered a violation of the rule. To avoid any such violations, you must ensure that your account balance/equity remains above $90,000.
Case 02:
Now, let's say you start with a $100,000 account and make a $4,000 profit. In this scenario, your Maximum Loss Limit will increase to $14,000 ($10,000 original limit + $4,000 profit). This means that you can sustain a total loss of $14,000, and if your account balance/equity ever drops below $90,000, it will be considered a violation of the rule.
Case 03:
Suppose you start with a $100,000 account, and after your trading cycle, you end up with a loss of $2,000 without any violations. This means your trading cycle will be
extended
, and you will continue trading under the same maximum loss limit with a balance of $98,000. It's important to note that in this scenario, your Maximum Loss Limit will not be reset in your extended cycle, and it will be reduced to $8,000 ($98,000–$90,000). Therefore, if your account balance/equity drops below $90,000 at any point during your trading journey, it will be considered a rule violation in both the Challenge Phase and the FundedNext Account Phase.
In summary, understanding the Maximum Loss Limit is crucial to managing your trading account. By keeping your account balance/equity above the 90% threshold, you can avoid any potential violations and ensure a successful trading journey.

title: How are the Daily Loss Limit (DLL) and Maximum Loss Limit (MLL) calculated on the FNL:002 12% MLL 3-Day Payout 2-Step 25K Challenge?
content:
TL;DR:
Daily Loss Limit = Initial Balance x 4%, and Maximum Loss Limit = Initial Balance x 12%, calculated the same way as FundedNext's Stellar 2-Step Challenge. Both limits are based on your $25,000 initial balance, and any profit you bank before the limit is checked increases how much you're allowed to lose at that point, in both the Challenge Phase and on the FundedNext Account.
How do I calculate my Daily Loss Limit (DLL)?
Formula:
Daily Loss Limit = Initial Balance x Daily Loss Limit Percentage (4%)
Swap charges, commissions, and fees are included in this calculation. Exceeding your Daily Loss Limit breaches your account.
Example 1
: With no profit yet that day:
$25,000 × 4% = $1,000 Daily Loss Limit
Example 2:
If you have made $500 in profit during the day:
$1,000 + $500 = $1,500 Daily Loss Limit
Losing more than $1,500 on closed or running trades that day would breach your Daily Loss Limit.
Your Daily Loss Limit resets every day at 00:00 (server time).
Once it resets, the previous day's profit no longer counts, and your Daily Loss Limit returns to being purely a percentage of your initial balance: $25,000 x 4% = $1,000.
Here is a
demonstration
of how daily loss limit calculation works.
How do I calculate my Maximum Loss Limit (MLL)?
Formula:
Maximum Loss Limit = Initial Balance x Maximum Loss Limit Percentage (12%)
Example 1:
On a $25,000 FNL:002 12% MLL 3-Day Payout 2-Step 25K Challenge account: $25,000 x 12% =
$3,000
Your account balance/equity must never drop below $25,000 minus $3,000 =
$22,000
. Dropping below this floor at any point, in the Challenge Phase or on the FundedNext Account, is a permanent breach of the account.
Example 2:
If you make $1,000 profit, your Maximum Loss Limit increases to $3,000 + $1,000 =
$4,000
. You can now sustain a total loss of $4,000 from your original $25,000 balance, since your equity floor still sits at $22,000. The $22,000 floor itself does not move; it's the dollar amount you're allowed to lose from your current position that grows as your profit grows.
Here is an
article
explaining how the maximum loss limit is calculated.
If either limit is exceeded, the account will be considered breached or violated. You can find more details on this
here.
Important note regarding server time
FundedNext's server follows a seasonal time adjustment: GMT+3 during Daylight Saving Time (typically the summer months) and GMT+2 for the rest of the year. Your Daily Loss Limit resets at 00:00 server time under this schedule.

title: What will happen to the maximum loss limit after a trader withdraws from a Stellar Instant Account?
content:
TLDR:
In Stellar Instant Accounts, the maximum loss limit follows a trailing method. It increases when you make profits and always stays at the highest level it has reached, capped at the account’s initial balance. After a withdrawal, the maximum loss limit does not reset lower; it continues at its strongest point. Depending on the withdrawal size, your equity may align more closely with the maximum loss limit, and in some cases, withdrawing the entire profit can bring your account right to that level.
The maximum loss limit in Stellar Instant is set at
6% below the initial balance
. For a $5,000 account, this means the starting maximum loss limit is $4,700.
As you build profits, the limit moves upward step by step:
If your highest profit is $200, then the maximum loss limit will be $4,900 ($4,700 + $200).
If you then lose $100, the limit stays at $4,900. Losses do not bring the limit down.
If your newest highest profit is $300, the limit moves to $5,000. Since the trailing maximum loss limit cannot go above the initial balance, it stays capped there. For more,
click here
.
Withdrawal Scenarios:
Scenario 1: Withdrawing the full profit at the cap
Suppose your balance grows to $5,500 (a $500 profit). The maximum loss limit is already capped at $5,000. If you withdraw the full $500, your balance goes back to $5,000, which equals the maximum loss limit. At this point, the account will be breached.
Scenario 2:
Withdrawing part of the profit
If you withdraw $300 while your balance is $5,500, your new balance is $5,200. The maximum loss limit remains at $5,000, leaving you a comfortable $200 buffer to continue trading.
Scenario 3:
Withdrawing when the limit has not yet reached the cap
Let’s say your $5,000 account grows by $200, making the balance $5,200. The maximum loss limit has moved up to $4,900. If you withdraw the $200 profit, the balance returns to $5,000, which is still $100 above the maximum loss limit. Your account remains fully safe and active.
Scenario 4:
Next cycles
After any withdrawal, a new trading cycle begins. Profits earned in the new cycle will continue to lift the maximum loss limit from its last highest point. For example, if your maximum loss limit is $4,900 after withdrawal and you earn another $10, it will count as the new highest balance, and the maximum loss limit moves to $4,910, and so on.
Key Takeaway:
The maximum loss limit always
progresses upward with your highest profit
and never decreases.
​
It is capped at the initial account balance.
​
Withdrawals simply bring your balance closer to the maximum loss limit, making thoughtful profit planning important for smooth trading.
​
Partial withdrawals provide a healthy space above the maximum loss limit, allowing you to continue trading confidently.

title: Understanding the KYC Verification Process at FundedNext
content:
TL;DR:
FundedNext uses a single, profile-level KYC system that covers all your accounts, CFDs, and futures at once. You'll need to verify after passing your Challenge Phase or before your first payout on a Stellar Instant Account. Your KYC must be fully
Approved
(not just
submitted
) to receive Performance Rewards, though you can keep trading in the meantime. Verification
expires every 90 days
and must be renewed to avoid payout restrictions. You get 3 submission attempts (5 for Iraq & Nigeria), so make sure your documents are ready before submitting.
At FundedNext, we prioritize security and compliance while ensuring a seamless experience for our traders. To streamline your journey, we have a centralized,
profile-level KYC
(Know Your Customer) system. This means your verification is tied to your profile rather than individual accounts, covering both CFDs and Futures product lines simultaneously.
What is Profile-Level KYC?
KYC is maintained at the profile level, creating a single source of truth for each trader. Once you have a verified KYC status on your profile, it applies to every account you hold, whether it is a Stellar 1-Step Account, a Stellar 2-Step Account, or a Stellar Instant Account. This eliminates the need for repetitive documentation and ensures a smoother transition between different Challenge Phases and FundedNext Accounts.
Once the KYC status for your profile has been updated, this is not limited to the CFD accounts; it is also applicable to your FundedNext Futures Accounts as well. To learn more about the FundedNext Futures KYC Verification requirements, please review
this article here
.
The "First-Trigger" Rule
If you hold both CFDs and Futures Accounts, whichever KYC trigger occurs first will establish the verified record for your entire profile. Once this is approved, you will not be required to complete a separate KYC for other product lines or other accounts you purchase in the future.
When is KYC required?
Traders are prompted to complete the KYC verification process at two specific stages:
Stellar Challenges (1-Step, 2-Step, and Lite Accounts)
On Stellar Challenge Accounts, you are required to submit your documents for KYC Verification after passing  the Challenge Phase/Phases. After you meet all the passing requirements for your Challenge you will have to wait for the
server reset
, and after that, your Challenge Account will be paused, and then you will be able to submit your KYC documents through the KYC Verification Center in your FundedNext Dashboard.
Stellar Instant Account
On Stellar Instant Accounts, you will be required to submit your documents for KYC Verification before requesting your first Performance Reward.
Verification States and Requirements
It is important to note that simply submitting your documents does not satisfy the KYC requirement. Your status must be "
Approved
" in order to move forward with your account or to request a Performance Reward. While your KYC is in "
Pending Review
" or "
Required
" status, you will be able to trade on a FundedNext Account and Stellar Instant Account; however, you will not be able to receive a Performance Reward from your account until the verification is successful, which is applicable for both Stellar FundedNext Accounts and Stellar Instant Accounts.
Required Documentation
To complete the KYC Verification, traders need to provide documents for identity verification. A photo of the physical copy of any of the following documents for KYC:
National ID
Passport
Permanent Residence Permit
Driving License
(applicable only for U.S.-based traders and traders from Australia, New Zealand and Canada)
Other than document submission, you also need to complete the
Liveness Check,
which is a real-time selfie to verify your identity.
Proof of Address (POA)
If requested, traders will have to submit proof of address to complete the KYC Verification process. To fulfill the address verification requirement, you must provide one of the following officially recognized documents:
Utility Bill
Bank Statement
Please ensure that the document submitted was issued within the last three months.
KYC Validity and Expiration
Mandatory 90-Day KYC Renewal
To ensure our records remain accurate and to prevent delays during Performance Reward processing, FundedNext requires a mandatory 90-day KYC renewal for all verified traders. Every trader must resubmit their KYC documents after 90 days of their last approval date when they become eligible for KYC.
Why is renewal required?
Proactive renewal helps catch issues such as expired documents, name mismatches, or changes in country of residence before they interfere with your Performance Reward requests. This ensures a smoother transition throughout your journey at FundedNext.
Renewal Timeline and Reminders
The 90-day clock begins the moment your KYC is approved. To help you stay compliant, the system provides the following notifications:
7 days before the verification expires
: You will receive an email and an in-app notification.
3 days before the verification expires
: You will receive a second email and an in-app banner.
1 day before the verification expires
: A final email and a non-dismissible banner will appear on your dashboard.
What happens if I am unable to submit the documents in time?
If you do not complete your KYC renewal after the 90-day window, you will still be able to continue trading on your FundedNext Account, or your Stellar Instant Account. However, you will not be able to request any Performance Reward from your account. Instead of the standard request process, you will see a prompt: "Verify your KYC to enable payouts." Once your renewal is approved, you can request your Performance Reward, and the 90-day cycle resets.
All other dashboard features, including account overviews, certificates (such as the Elite Trader Certificate), and notifications, remain fully accessible.
Submission Attempts and Document Rules
The number of allowed KYC submission attempts can vary based on the local regulations and provider requirements:
Iraq and Nigeri
a: 5 attempts
All Other Countries
: 3 attempts.
Exhausted Attempts
If you exhaust all your attempts, please contact
our support team
, and we will guide you accordingly.

title: Is News Trading Allowed in the Stellar Instant Accounts?
content:
TL;DR:
Yes, news trading is allowed in the Stellar Instant Account, but trades executed within 5 minutes before or after a listed high-impact news event are subject to the
News Profit Split Rule
. Under this rule, only
40% of the profit
from those trades will count toward your account’s profit. This adjustment applies to both market and pending orders and can affect Performance Rewards eligibility and account metrics. FundedNext also applies a
1% equity buffer
to the Trailing Maximum Loss Limit (MLL) to prevent unintended breaches caused by news-time profit deductions.
Yes, news trading is allowed in the Stellar Instant model.
Traders can open or close trades during high-impact news events. However, a special News Profit Rule applies during these events.
News Profit Rule
Time Window:
This rule applies to all trades executed within a 10-minute window—5 minutes before and 5 minutes after a listed high-impact news event.
Profit Calculation:
Only
40% of the profit
from trades placed during this window will be counted toward your account’s profit.
Applies To:
Market executions (opening or closing a trade)
Pending orders (triggered via Take Profit or Stop Loss)
Important Clarifications:
This rule only applies to the FundedNext Stellar Instant Accounts.
Partial Order Closures:
If part of a position is closed during the news window, the entire trade is affected, and only 40% of the profit will count.
Impact on Metrics:
This adjustment may reduce the net profit shown in your account.
News Profit is calculated after the cycle ends.
Example Calculation:
A trader ends their cycle with $10,000 profit, excluding news trades.
They also made $3,000 profit from trades executed during the news window.
As per the rule:
40% of the $3,000 = $1,200
So, the total profit counted will be $(10,000 + 1,200) = $11,200
1% News Time MLL Equity Adjustment—Explained with Example
Let’s walk through a scenario to understand how we apply a 1% buffer to the Trailing Maximum Loss Limit (MLL) Equity when News Time profit impacts the withdrawal and equity threshold.
Example Breakdown
Starting Balance:
$10,000
Initial Trailing MLL Equity:
$9,400
Trade Outcomes:
Non-News Trade P/L:
-$500
News Time Trade P/L:
+$1,200
Final Balance:
$10,700
Updated MLL Equity:
After the profit, the
Trailing MLL Equity
rises to match the starting balance:
$10,000
Withdrawal & News Adjustment:
Since the current balance is $10,700 and the MLL Equity is $10,000, the trader is eligible to withdraw a maximum of $700.
However, here's the News Time Reward Share:
60% of News Profit
goes to FundedNext
60% of $1,200 =
$720
Now, when we deduct this $720 from the wallet (which reflects on the balance):
New Balance = $10,700 - $720 = $9,980
This new balance of $9,980
falls below
the updated MLL Equity of $10,000, causing a
breach
.
🛡️
Applying a 1% Safety Buffer
To prevent such an unintended breach due to news-time profit adjustments, we offer a
1% equity extension
to the Trailing MLL.
Extended MLL Equity:
$10,000 →
$9,900
So now, even after the wallet deduction, the account remains
safe
:
Final Adjusted Balance:
$9,980
New MLL Equity:
$9,900 → ✅ No Breach
New Cycle Starts From:
Starting Balance:
$10,000
Trailing MLL Equity (with 1% buffer):
$9,900
This small but significant buffer ensures fairness and protects traders from technical breaches caused by the timing of reward shares during news events. This 1% buffer, the trader will get a maximum of 3 times in one single account.

title: When does the Daily Loss Limit reset with FundedNext CFD?
content:
TL;DR:
The
Daily Loss Limit at FundedNext resets at midnight based on server time
. When daylight saving time is active, the server operates on
GMT+3
, so the reset occurs at
00:00 GMT+3
. When daylight saving time is not in effect, the server runs on
GMT+2
, and the reset occurs at
00:00 GMT+2
. The exact reset countdown can always be tracked directly from the dashboard.
Traders are obligated to adhere to the Daily Loss Limit and Maximum Loss Limit rules when engaging in trading activities with FundedNext.
The Daily Loss Limit resets at midnight, based on the server's time. Please note that the server time changes depending on whether daylight saving time is in effect or not.
During daylight saving time, which typically occurs during the summer months, the server time is set to Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) +3. This means the daily loss limit resets at midnight GMT+3.
For the remainder of the year, when daylight saving time is not in effect, the server time is adjusted to GMT+2. In this case, the daily loss limit resets at midnight GMT+2.
Traders can easily monitor the countdown timer for the Daily Loss Limit reset on their dashboard to ensure they stay informed and compliant with our established trading regulations.

title: Is there an inactivity period for my accounts in FundedNext CFD?
content:
TL;DR:
Accounts on FundedNext, including Stellar 1-Step, Stellar 2-Step, Stellar Lite, and Stellar Instant Accounts, expire after 30 days of inactivity. Log in and trade to stay active. No extensions or customizations are available. KYC Verification must be completed within 30 days post Challenge, or the account will be deactivated.
FundedNext will count a trading account to be expired, and the system will mark the account as inactive if a trader does not place a trade on the account for 30 consecutive calendar days, which means weekends and holidays are also included in this 30 days timeframe. After this time period, the system will mark the account as deactivated. To avoid this, traders can simply execute a trade within a period of 30 days.​
Can I extend the inactivity period or customize it to suit my needs?
FundedNext does not offer the option to extend or customize the inactivity period, and the policy applies uniformly to all accounts. The inactivity period of 30 consecutive days is a standard policy to ensure active participation and consistent platform performance.
Can I request a new account after expiration?
Traders whose accounts have expired due to inactivity can reach out to FundedNext Support regarding the issuance of a new account. However, whether a replacement account is provided will be determined by FundedNext based on the specific situation.
​
Are there any fees associated with account expiration?
There are no fees associated with issuing a new account to replace one that has expired due to inactivity. Reissuing an account remains subject to FundedNext’s review of your specific case.

title: What Is the Eligibility Criteria for My Performance Reward in the Stellar Instant Account?
content:
TL;DR:
In the Stellar Instant Account, you can claim your Performance Reward  either
on-demand
by achieving 5% account growth or on a
bi-weekly (14-day) cycle
if growth is less than 5%, provided you meet the minimum 1% growth requirement.
Performance Rewards in Stellar Instant can be accessed in two ways: on-demand when reaching 5% growth, or after 14 days for any growth above 1%.
1. On-Demand Performance Reward (Anytime)
You can request your Performance Reward once your account reaches 5% growth—but eligibility is confirmed at the End of Day (EOD).
​
The system checks your account eligibility at
the End of Day (EOD)
.
If your account meets the
5% growth milestone at the time of the EOD check
, the
Transfer to Wallet
option is enabled.
The option remains available
until you place a new trade
.
Once a trade is placed during the current trading day, the transfer option is
disabled immediately
.
It will remain disabled until the
next EOD eligibility check
.
At the next EOD, the system will re-evaluate eligibility:
​
If the account still meets the 5% growth requirement, the option is re-enabled.
If not, it remains disabled.
Example:
​
Starting balance:
$10,000
Profit:
$500 (5% growth)
If your account meets 5% growth at Monday’s EOD, you can transfer your reward.
If you place a trade on Tuesday before transferring, the option will be disabled. It will be checked again at Tuesday’s EOD and re-enabled only if 5% growth is still maintained.
2. Bi-Weekly (14-Day) Performance Reward
If your growth is
less than 5%
but
at least 1%
, you can withdraw Rewards 14 days after your cycle’s start date.
​
This option is useful if you want regular payouts without hitting the 5% growth target.
Example:
Starting balance = $10,000
Profit = $300 (3% growth) → Eligible for withdrawal after 14 days.
Important:
The minimum growth requirement for any Reward is
1%
.
If growth is below 1%, you cannot request a Reward.

title: What is slippage? Understanding Slippage in Trading
content:
Slippage is a natural occurrence in trading and not something to be seen as entirely negative. It occurs when a trading order is executed at a price different from the one initially requested, and it is a normal part of participating in a dynamic and fast-moving market.
Just as legendary investor Warren Buffett once remarked, "
The true investor welcomes volatility. A wildly fluctuating market means that irrationally low prices will periodically be attached to solid businesses.
"
While forex trading differs from investing in stocks, the underlying principle remains the same: volatility, though challenging, often creates opportunities. Similarly, slippage, though sometimes seen as negative, is a normal aspect of a fast-moving market that reflects its dynamic nature.
To execute a trade, there must be sufcient
price and volume availability
in the market. If the requested price is not available due to market conditions, the order is executed at the
next best available price.
This naturally leads to slippage, particularly during periods of high volatility or low liquidity.
Why Does Slippage Occur?
Slippage typically occurs during periods of high volatility or low liquidity, such as major news announcements or market openings, where rapid price movements are common. Executing a high-lot trade can also cause slippage, as it may quickly use up the available liquidity at the quote price and lead to the remaining volume being filled at a less favorable price. Sometimes there can be
sudden
volume surges
in the market.  In these environments, if the market cannot meet the desired price of the trader due to insufficiant liquidity, orders are executed at the next best available price. The difference between the requested price and the execution price creates slippage.
Slippage After a Market Gap:
A
market gap
occurs when there is a significant price difference between the closing price of one trading session and the opening price of the next, typically caused by major news or
events after market closure
. These gaps are a
normal
part of market dynamics but can lead to unexpected outcomes for traders.
At FundedNext, we are not responsible for any issues resulting from market gaps, as they are a natural part of real market conditions. Therefore, we cannot offer any adjustments for such occurrences.
Click here to learn more
.
A Note to Our Traders
At FundedNext, we are committed to delivering reliable service and ensuring efficient trade execution under simulated
real market environment
. It is important to understand that
slippage is a natural aspect
of trading and reflects the natural behavior of financial markets, especially during
high-impact news
events. To maintain a fair and transparent simulated trading environment, we replicate real market conditions so that traders experience conditions similar to those they would face in
live markets
. As part of this, slippage, which naturally occurs in the market, will also be present.
While slippage is unavoidable, we work hard to support our traders in navigating uncertainties. However, any cases of slippage during high-impact news releases will not be addressed unless it is a total execution failure.
Adjustments will only be considered for trades placed after 10 minutes of the news publication.
Understanding and accepting slippage is essential for developing a professional trading mindset. Rather than seeing it as a setback,
successful traders
recognize slippage as a natural part of trading in dynamic markets. At
FundedNext
, we encourage our traders to adopt this perspective, enabling them to stay focused on refining their strategies, managing risks effectively, and making confident, informed decisions in any market condition.

title: Is trading in the FundedNext Challenge and FundedNext Account conducted according to the real market?
content:
Yes. Your orders on FundedNext execute in a simulated real market environment, with quotes using
FundedNext's liquidity providers
. The order will be filled according to the prevailing market conditions, order book, and availability of the required volume at that price—the
same mechanics you’d expect in a real trading environment.
What does that mean for you?
Best available price:
When you hit buy/sell, your order fills at the best available price in the book—no artificial “requotes.”
​
Slippage
is real:
In fast or thin markets (news, rollovers, off-hours), you might get filled a few pips away from your click. This can result in less favorable fills—exactly like real markets.
​
Volatility matters:
Wider spreads and thinner liquidity during high-impact moments can increase price differences between request and fill.
Thus, the discrepancy between the requested price and the filled price of an order is not unique to our platform—it's a common experience in trading, regardless of the firm, brokerage, or any financial markets.
​
Fair pipeline:
No manual price shading—execution is driven by simulated real market quotes using FundedNext's liquidity providers and the order book.
​
Execution assurance
: Orders are routed to Real LP quotes and filled at the best available market price at that moment—no manipulation, just real market mechanics.
It is important to note that, in volatile and/or illiquid markets, the difference between request and execution prices might vary from usual.
For instance, during news releases or market rollovers, spreads tend to widen considerably, also creating a void in the order book and volume availability. This results in a price difference, which can occur in both negative and positive directions.

EA usage fee to FundedNext.

Traders are required to customize their EA or bot settings to align with their unique trading styles.
Each EA or bot is required to employ a distinct strategy, avoiding identical trades across any accounts within FundedNext.
There is a maximum allocation limit of $300,000 for each EA or trading bot's strategy.
Using EA that incorporates third-party applications such as Telegram or WhatsApp is strictly prohibited.
Any tools that do not execute trades but instead only modify trade parameters such as Stop Loss (SL), Take Profit (TP), or lot size calculations are also classified as EAs. Consequently, traders must comply with all existing FundedNext EA rules while using them.

title: What are the requirements for requesting a Payout on the FNL:002 12% MLL 3-Day Payout 2-Step 25K Challenge?
content:
TL;DR:
To request your Performance Reward on the FundedNext Account, you need at least 3 profitable days, each with a minimum of 1% profit ($250 on a $25,000 account). These days do not need to be consecutive. You keep an 85% Reward Share. You must withdraw the full amount; partial withdrawals are not allowed, and your next cycle cannot start until you do.
What is a Profitable Day and how does it work?
A Profitable Day is a trading day where your closed trades generate a net profit that meets or exceeds the minimum profit target. Profit is attributed to the day the trade closes, regardless of when it was opened.
Minimum requirement:
On a $25,000 account, a Profitable Day requires at least $250 in net profit from closed trades ($25,000 × 1%).
Challenge Phase:
Profitable Days count toward passing each phase.
Phase 1: 2 Profitable Days required
Phase 2: 2 Profitable Days required
FundedNext Account:
Once you reach the FundedNext Account, you need 3 Profitable Days within a single reward cycle to be eligible to request your Performance Reward.
Example
Let's break down closed trades day by day to see which ones qualify as Profitable Days (minimum $250 net profit from closed trades):
Day
Closed Trades P&L
Profitable Day Reached?
Completed Profitable Days
Profitable Day Calculation
Day 1
+$270 (Trades Opened: 2, Trades Closed: 2)
YES (+$270 >= $250)
1
Day 1 is calculated based on the 2 trades that closed on Day 1 with a $270 profit. As $270 is greater than $250, Day 1 counts as a Profitable Day.
Day 2
+$150 (Trades Opened: 3, Trades Closed: 3)
NO (+$150 < $250)
1
Day 2 is calculated based on the 3 trades that closed on Day 2 with a $150 profit. As $150 is less than $250, Day 2 does not count as a Profitable Day.
Day 3
+$300 closed, +$150 floating (Trades Opened: 6, Trades Closed Today: 4, Trades Running: 2)
YES
2
Day 3 is calculated based on the 4 trades that closed on Day 3 with a $300 profit. As $300 is greater than $250, Day 3 counts as a Profitable Day. Since 2 trades are still running, their floating profits ($150) aren't counted.
Day 4
+$260 (Trades Opened Today: 2, Previous Day Trades Closed: 2, Today's Trades Closed: 4)
YES
3
Day 4 is calculated based on the 4 trades that closed on Day 4 with a $260 profit. As $260 is greater than $250, Day 4 counts as a Profitable Day.
After Day 4, this trader has reached 3 Profitable Days within the reward cycle and is eligible to request a payout.
Does News Trading profit count toward my Profitable Day?
News trading is not allowed on the FNL:002 12% MLL 3-Day Payout 2-Step 25K Challenge. If a trade is flagged as news trading, 100% of the profit from that trade is deducted from your account as a rule violation.
However, that flagged profit is
still counted toward your Profitable Day calculation
for the day it closed. This means a trading day can still qualify as a Profitable Day if your total closed profit, including any profit later flagged and deducted for news trading, meets the $250 (1%) minimum, even though you don't keep that portion of the profit.
How many Profitable Days do I need at each stage?
Stage
Minimum Profitable Days Required
Challenge Phase 1
2 days
Challenge Phase 2
2 days
FundedNext Account (for Payout)
3 days, not necessarily consecutive
Profitable Days do not need to be consecutive at any stage. You can reach your total on any day throughout the phase or reward cycle.
What is my Reward Share?
You keep
85%
of the profit you generate on your FundedNext Account.
Learn more about how you can withdraw your reward share by clicking
here
.
What happens once I meet the Payout requirements?
You'll receive a pop-up prompting you to transfer your profit to your wallet.
Once transferred, you must request the full profit amount for payout, minus any profit flagged for a rule violation.
Partial Performance Reward requests are not possible; you must withdraw the entire eligible amount at once.
When does my next reward cycle start?
Your new cycle begins fresh at your initial account balance only after you complete the wallet transfer. If you don't transfer your profit to your wallet, your current cycle keeps running; it will not reset or restart until the transfer is made.

title: What is the minimum Performance Reward limit for FundedNext?
content:
The minimum Performance Reward limit for FundedNext is determined based on the reward amount and your desired available payout methods.
If the Performance Reward amount is below $20, you will not be able to place a Performance Reward request for that cycle. The amount will be carried forward and adjusted with the next Performance Reward.​
​
If the Performance Reward amount is $20 or more, you can request your Reward through USDT (TRC20 and ERC20). The highest Performance Reward amount for USDT (TRC20 and ERC20) is $1,999.​
If the Performance Reward amount is $20 or more, you can request your Reward through USDC (ERC20). The highest Performance Reward amount for USDC (ERC20) is $1,999.​
​
RiseWorks Performance Rewards can be requested from a minimum of $50, with no maximum limit applied.
If you are from the non-OFAC (Office of Foreign Assets Control) countries and RiseWorks is available, you can request your Performance Reward through USDT (ERC20) and USDC (ERC20). The highest Performance Reward amount for USDT (ERC20) and USDC (ERC20) is $1,999. However, the lowest Performance Reward amount for USDT (ERC20) and USDC (ERC20) is $20.
​
If you are from the OFAC (Office of Foreign Assets Control) countries and RiseWorks is unavailable, you can request your Performance Reward through USDT (ERC20) and USDC (ERC20). The highest Performance Reward amount for USDT (ERC20) and USDC (ERC20) is $1,000,000.
​
Performance Rewards can be requested using the bank transfer method from $1,000 to $50,000.
TC Pay (Exclusively for Iranian Traders only)
Additionally, exclusively for traders from Iran, they have the option to request their Performance Reward using TC Pay. The minimum amount that can be requested using TC Pay is $20, and the maximum amount is $50,000.
How does the adjustment of outstanding profit work (if the account is breached)?
If you have a withdrawable profit below $20 in your account but breach it in the next trading cycle, the outstanding profit from the last trading cycle will be adjusted and processed. This allows you to receive your accumulated earnings. To initiate the adjustment, you can contact the FundedNext Support Team, who will assist in processing the Performance Reward request.
Please note that these policies are subject to change, and the latest information can be found on our website.
​
Is there a processing fee for Performance Reward requests?
Yes, a processing fee is applied to all Performance Reward requests to cover the transaction costs and associated charges incurred during the Performance Reward process. Here's how it works:
For Performance Rewards processed through RiseWork, a processing fee of up to 3.5% is applied.
​
For Performance Rewards using other methods, a processing fee of up to 3.5% is also applied.
The fee is determined by the payment provider and remains consistent, regardless of the reward share amount, whether you're requesting $100 or $10,000. The exact fee may vary based on the payout method selected, the payment provider's terms, and prevailing market conditions. Please note that no additional charges are added to your Performance Reward or payout request.

title: Is there any Consistency Rule in the FNL: 001 NO DLL 1-Step CFDs 50K Account?
content:
TL;DR:
The 40% Consistency Rule ensures your trading is stable and repeatable. No single trading day's profit cannot exceed 40% of your total profit target. If it does, your account is not breached — instead, your total profit target automatically increases to bring that day back within the 40% ratio.
What is the 40% Consistency Rule?
The rule requires that no single trading day's profit does not make up more than 40% of your overall profit target. It is designed to encourage steady, disciplined trading habits.
Does the consistency rule apply to both the Challenge Phase and the FundedNext Phase?
There is a consistency rule for the FNL: 001 NO DLL 1-Step CFDs 50K Challenge Phase. However, there is no consistency rule for the
FNL: 001 NO DLL 1-Step CFDs 50K FundedNext Phase
.
How is the daily profit limit calculated?
On a standard
$50,000 account
, your initial profit target is
$3,000
.
To find your daily profit limit,
multiply the target by 40%
.
Daily Profit Limit: $3,000 x 40% =
$1,200
.
As long as your daily profits stay at or below
$1,200
, your account maintains the consistency rule and your target stays at
$3,000
.
What happens if I make more than required profit in a single day?
If you make a larger profit than the required profit,
you do not fail the Challenge Phase
. Instead, your overall profit target scales up to keep that large trading day mathematically aligned with the 40% rule.
Your new required target is calculated by dividing your highest profit day by 40% ($0.40).
Examples of Target Adjustments
Here is how your total profit target shifts if you experience multiple high-profit days:
Scenario
Single-Day Profit
Target Adjustment Formula
New Total Profit Target
Baseline
Up to $1,200
No adjustment needed
$3,000
First Day
(Profit limit: $1200)
$1,400
$1,400 divided by 40%
$3,500
Second Day
(Profit limit: $3500 x 40% = $1400)
$1,450
$1,450 divided by 40%
$3,625
Key Takeaway
If your profit limit increases, you simply need to keep trading and accumulating smaller, consistent profitable days until your total net profit reaches the new adjusted profit target. Your account stays open and active the entire time.

title: What is the pip or point value in FundedNext?
content:
Understanding pip or point value is essential in forex trading, as it plays a pivotal role in managing your risk and estimating your potential gains or losses.
What Are Points, Pips, and Pipettes?
In trading,
Points,
Pips,
and
Pipettes
are essential terms used to measure
price movements
in various markets, such as forex, commodities, indices, and crypto. These terms help traders assess and communicate the extent of price changes with precision, ensuring a clear understanding of market fluctuations.
1. Point
A
Point
refers to a
full unit change
in price. This is typically used for larger price movements, particularly in commodities and indices.
Example for US30
:
If the price of
US30
moves from
35,000.10
to
35,001.10
, the change is
1 point
. This is a 1-point move, representing a full unit shift in value.
2. Pip
A
pip
stands for
"percentage in point"
and is the standard unit for measuring price movements in most currency pairs. A pip represents the
smallest price movement
that an asset can make in the market.
Example for EURUSD
:
If the price of the
EURUSD
pair moves from
1.10000
to
1.10010
, it has moved by
1 pip.
For most currency pairs like
EURUSD
, a pip is equal to a
0.0001
price movement.
​
Example for USDJPY
:
For the
USDJPY
pair, a pip represents a
0.01
change. So, if the price moves from
110.101
to
110.111
, that’s a
1-pip
movement.
3. Pipette
A
pipette
is
one-tenth of a pip
and allows for even more precise measurements of price movements, which is especially useful for high-frequency or low-volatility assets.
Example for EURUSD
:
A
pipette
would be a
0.00001
change in price. For example, if the
EURUSD
pair moves from
1.10001
to
1.10002
, that’s a
1-pipette
move.
​
Example for USDJPY
:
In the
USDJPY
pair, a
pipette
represents a
0.001
change in price. A move from
110.101
to
110.102
is a
1-pipette
movement.
The value of a pip or a point isn't static; it changes depending on the currency pair, commodities, and indices you're trading. Below, you will find a comprehensive chart detailing the pip or point value for all forex instruments, calculated based on 1 standard lot size, to guide you through this essential aspect.
How do I calculate the potential profit or loss for my trades in FundedNext?
To determine the profit or loss for a particular currency pair, commodities, indices, and cryptocurrencies, use the following formula:
Profit/Loss =
Pip/Point Difference x Lot Size x Pip Value.
Example 1: Buying 1 lot EURUSD
​
Open Price: 1.09220
Close Price: 1.09320
Lot Size: 1 lot
Pip Difference: 10 Pips or 100 Pippetes
Profit/loss = (10 Pips x 1 Lot x $10.00) = +$100.00
​
​
Outcome:
As the trader initiated a buy trade on EURUSD at an opening price of 1.09220 and closed the trade at 1.09320, the pip difference for the trade was 10 pips. In this instance, the trader would gain a profit of +$100.00 from this specific trade.
Example 2: Buying 1 lot XAUUSD
​
Open Price: 1892.00
Close Price: 1892.70
Lot Size: 1 lot
Pip Difference: 7 Pips or 70 Pippetes
Profit/loss = (7 Pips x 1 Lot x $10.00) = +$70.00
​
​
Outcome:
As the trader initiated a buy trade on XAUUSD at an opening price of 1892.00 and closed the trade at 1892.70, the pip difference for the trade was 7 pips. In this instance, the trader would gain a profit of +$70.00 from this specific trade.
Example 3: Selling 1 lot US30
​
Open Price: 34567.10
Close Price: 34562.10
Lot Size: 1 lot
Point Difference: 5 Points or 50 Pips
Profit/loss = (5 Points x 1 Lot x $10.00) = +$50.00
​
​
Outcome:
As the trader initiated a sell trade on US30 at an opening price of 34567.10 and closed the trade at 34562.10, the point difference for the trade was 5 points. In this instance, the trader would gain a profit of +$50.00 from this specific trade.
Example 4: Selling 1 lot BTCUSD
​
Open Price: 52206.10
Close Price: 52203.10
Lot Size: 1 lot
Point Difference: 30 Pips
Profit/loss = (30 Pips x 1 Lot x $0.10) = +$3.00
​
​
Outcome:
As the trader initiated a sell trade on BTCUSD at an opening price of 52206.10 and closed the trade at 52203.10, the pip difference for the trade was 30 pips. In this instance, the trader would gain a profit of +$3.00 from this specific trade.
Example 5:
May 2025: Selling 1 lot AUDCAD
Open Price: 0.90000
Close Price: 0.89200
Lot Size: 1 lot
Point Difference: 80 Pips
Profit/loss = (80 Pips x 1 Lot x $7.14) =
+$571.20
Outcome:
With an 80-pip move on AUDCAD in May 2025, where the pip value was
$7.14
, the trade returned a profit of
$571.20
.
August 2025: Selling 1 lot AUDCAD
Open Price: 0.90000
Close Price: 0.89200
Lot Size: 1 lot
Point Difference: 80 Pips
Profit/loss = (80 Pips x 1 Lot x $7.28) =
+$582.40
Outcome:
In August 2025, the identical 80-pip move yielded
$582.40
because the pip value is
$7.28
, showing how changes in pip value over time alter P&L even when the pip distance is the same.
These examples are designed to provide a clear understanding of how pip values or point values impact your trading outcomes. Remember, the key to successful trading lies not just in understanding these calculations but also in applying them effectively to your trading strategy. Please also note that for some instruments, pip values can differ slightly depending on the conversion rate.

title: Does FundedNext offer a Scale-Up plan?
content:
For Stellar Challenges Purchased or Reset Before January 12, 2026
Traders with Stellar Challenges purchased or reset before January 12, 2026 will continue to follow the previous Scale-Up plan criteria, even if they pass the Challenge and receive their FundedNext Account after January 12, 2026.
For Stellar Challenges Purchased or Reset After January 12, 2026
Traders with Stellar Challenges purchased or reset after January 12, 2026 will follow the
new Scale-Up plan.
FundedNext provides a Scale-Up plan for traders who consistently demonstrate success and follow the trading rules.
The Scale-Up plan presents traders with an opportunity to expand their trading activity by potentially receiving a simulated capital allocation of up to $4 million. Skilled and disciplined traders seeking to elevate their trading endeavors can benefit from FundedNext's Scale-Up plan. The eligibility criteria for the Evaluation, Express, Stellar  1-Step, Stellar 2-Step, or Stellar Lite Accounts remain consistent to simplify the process. The trader must ensure that all trades are closed and should contact support immediately after completing their trading cycle before initiating any new trades.
Review Process & Eligibility Criteria:
To be considered for scaling up, traders must meet the following eligibility criteria in a FundedNext Account over a four-month period:
Achieve a minimum accumulated disbursed amount growth of 10% in four consecutive months.
Receive at least two Performance Reward within these successive four months.
The last trading cycle should end in profit.
FundedNext Accounts (Evaluation, Express, Stellar or Stellar Lite) undergo a review every four months. Traders who meet the eligibility criteria are eligible for a 40% increase in the account balance, up to a maximum of 4 million.
Based on the trader's performance over the four consecutive months and if all other criteria are met, FundedNext will review the trader's account and potentially Scale the account size up by 40%. So, with the 40% Scale-Up, the new balance is $140,000.
Therefore, considering the new account balance:
The daily loss limit is 5% (4% in Stellar Lite Accounts and 3% in Stellar 1-Step Accounts), which amounts to $7,000 ($5,600 in Stellar Lite and $4,200 in Stellar 1-Step).
The maximum loss limit is 10% (8% in Stellar Lite Accounts and 6% in Stellar 1-Step Accounts), which equates to $14,000 ($11,200 in Stellar Lite and $8,400 in Stellar 1-Step).
The new scale-up target for the next four months is a 10% disbursed amount growth of $140,000.
Scaling up with FundedNext is a straightforward process that opens doors to enhanced opportunities for traders.
What if a trader managed to reach 10% of their disbursed amount for scaling up but was unable to make a profit in the last trading cycle?
For instance, let's consider a trader who began trading on January 1st. After four consecutive months (January, February, March, and April), the trader managed to achieve a 10% disbursed amount growth by the end of April. However, during the last trading cycle, the trader was unable to end in profit. As the trader was unable to end his last trading cycle in profit, the trader will not be eligible for the Scale-Up plan. In such a scenario, the trader's account will be evaluated again in May, following the completion of their trading cycle (February, March, April, and May). Essentially, if the trader meets all the criteria during the most recent four-month period, they will be eligible for the Scale-Up plan.
